A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PosterForest and contain readable methods, equations, empirical results, figures, and appendices. The revised material can be reliably matched across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original automatic evaluations, a 22-participant human study, qualitative comparisons, and ablations in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 reports automatic evaluations, a 25-participant human study, revised qualitative outputs, and ablations in Section 4 and the appendices.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.3 replace MLLM-based layout initialization with deterministic initialization from content statistics. The explicit analysis, opinion-exchange, and finalization procedure becomes type-specific content/layout updates conditioned on updated parents and descendants, with structured global feedback informing further traversal. These are substantive procedural revisions.

E1.justification: Both retain the 100-pair Paper2Poster benchmark and 15 additional AI paper–poster pairs, covering computer vision, NLP, and reinforcement learning. Figure A1 replaces the LabelDistill example with YOLO-World, already represented in the hierarchy ablation; this does not establish expanded task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain their comparator sets, including GPT-4o direct-generation methods, OWL, PPTAgent, P2P, and Paper2Poster/PosterAgent where applicable. The qualitative comparisons also retain their baseline membership. The new training-free column does not introduce a comparator.

E3.justification: Section 4.4 and Appendix C.2 increase the human-study sample from 22 to 25 participants. The ten poster sets, four compared methods, and four assessment criteria remain. Benchmark splits, automatic metrics, and poster-format controls are retained.

E4.justification: The hierarchy and content/layout-agent ablation questions remain, but Figures 5–6 show revised generated outputs and Section 4.5 revises the discussed failure behavior. No new ablation axis or robustness suite appears. Appendix D and Figure A3 retain the clustered-figure parsing failure case.

E5.justification: Both Appendix B.3 passages state that Python, NumPy, and PyTorch seeds were fixed. Both report aggregate scores and preference percentages without confidence intervals, repeated-run uncertainty summaries, or significance tests. The participant-count increase does not change uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises the preference percentages: PosterForest's content preference changes from 53.2% to 56.0% and overall preference from 58.2% to 59.2%; Paper2Poster's overall preference changes from 26.9% to 27.2%. Figures 4–6 and A1–A2 also revise qualitative outputs. Table 1 scores remain identical. The changed method and study sample preclude interpreting these as same-setting gains.

T1.justification: Section 3 expands the mathematical definitions of tree nodes and attributes and replaces opinion-exchange equations with parent/descendant-conditioned updates and a feedback-continuation rule. This revises the algorithm's formal specification, without adding theoretical guarantees, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The principal contributions remain a training-free PosterForest framework, a hierarchical Poster Tree, coordinated content/layout refinement, and favorable automatic and human evaluations. The revised abstract and numerical preference summary retain these claims rather than establishing a new contribution scope.

C2.justification: Section 4.5 shifts the Content Agent explanation from eliminating overflow toward pruning cross-node redundancy, and adds suboptimal figure scaling to the layout-only failure interpretation. Section 3 more explicitly explains propagation of global constraints through the hierarchy. The substantive limitations and future directions remain largely unchanged.

D1.justification: New Appendix E and Figures A4–A8 provide prompts for parsing, summarization, content refinement, layout refinement, and feedback, including input/output schemas, text-fill targets, and layout-adjustment rules. This substantially expands implementation documentation. The hardware, software environment, and code-access URL are retained.

R1.justification: v2 removes the Du et al. and Liang et al. multi-agent-debate references and the Gemini reference by Team et al. (2023). Section 3.1 also changes its description of Paper2Poster's feedback loop from panel-layout refinement to content refinement within panels. The broader related-work coverage remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution narrative, and substantial portions of Section 3 are rewritten and reorganized around hierarchical traversal. v2 separates Limitations from the conclusion, adds Ethical Considerations and Acknowledgments, and introduces a structured agent-prompt appendix. These extend beyond local language corrections.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn; Figures 5–6 gain colored highlights and enlarged detail panels; Table 1 gains a training-free column; and Algorithm 1 is removed. New Figures A4–A8 display agent prompts, alongside widespread changes to figure placement and document layout.

improvement.justification: Appendix E's concrete prompts and Section 3's explicit update dependencies improve implementation transparency, while enlarged ablation details make the evidence easier to inspect. These support a limited overall quality gain. The modest human-study expansion and unchanged automatic scores do not establish superior performance of the revised procedure.
